clue.text: Contests work against models

indicators.note: against means next to or leaning on, so one piece is set right beside the other

parts.note: OP is the standard abbreviation for opus, a work
models, as a verb, means poses, as a sitter does for an artist

explanation.surface: Someone challenges a job done in opposition to certain fashion models.
explanation.definitionFit: To contest a claim or a motion is to stand against it, to resist it.

clue.text: See 6
Doorman's drink

definitions.meaning: a person who guards the door of a hotel or college
a dark beer brewed from roasted malt

explanation.surface: The doorkeeper's tipple.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', linking the two definitions; the answer also suggests Cole Porter, the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotel's door attendant is called by this name, and it is also a dark stout-like beer.

clue.text: Not immediately thinking about ignoring the alarm clock?

definitions.meaning: deferring a decision until the next day, as in to do so on an idea
staying asleep after the alarm sounds, literally carrying on in slumber

explanation.surface: Putting off a decision by lying in when the alarm rings.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means postponing a decision overnight, and literally it means continuing to slumber past waking time.

clue.text: Astronomer Newton putting narrative first

indicators.note: putting the narrative first means it comes before the letter for Newton

parts.note: a saga is a long narrative or tale
N is the symbol for the newton, the unit of force

explanation.surface: The astronomer Isaac Newton tells a story before anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Newton' tempts as the astronomer himself; it is the unit, giving N.
explanation.definitionFit: Carl Sagan was an American astronomer and popular science writer, presenter of Cosmos.

clue.text: Biblical figure's end, after brief record period

indicators.note: after places the word for end behind the record and period pieces

parts.note: an EP, extended play, is a short record
HR is the abbreviation for hour, a period of time
an end is an aim or goal, as in means to an end

explanation.surface: A Bible character's death comes after a short spell on record.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after 'figure' is 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Ephraim was a son of Joseph in Genesis and gave his name to one of the tribes of Israel.

clue.text: Duke, having lost weight, is a quite different duke

indicators.note: having lost means without, so the letter for weight is dropped

parts.note: the Duke of Wellington was the British general who won at Waterloo

explanation.surface: A slimmed-down aristocrat becomes another nobleman entirely.
explanation.definitionFit: Duke Ellington was the jazz bandleader and composer, a duke only by nickname.

clue.text: Penthouse-style work situation coveted by ambitious politicians?

definitions.text: Penthouse-style work situation coveted by ambitious politicians?

parts.words: Penthouse-style work situation coveted by ambitious politicians?
parts.note: literally a workplace at the top of a tall building, and figuratively a senior government post that politicians aim for

explanation.surface: Politicians on the make covet a top-floor workplace.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means an important public position, such as a ministerial post, and literally a workplace far up.

clue.text: Lymphatic tissue helps to hide malformed node

indicators.note: to hide means to conceal inside, so the helps word wraps round the other letters

parts.note: aids means helps

indicators.note: malformed means badly shaped, so the letters of node are reshaped

explanation.surface: A medical note: some lymph tissue serves to conceal a misshapen node.
explanation.walkthrough: 'helps' looks like a verb in the surface, but it is the synonym that does the hiding.
explanation.definitionFit: Adenoids are masses of lymph tissue at the back of the nose, often removed in children.

clue.text: Imagine seeing something in yours!

parts.note: imagining something is picturing it inwardly, visualising with the imagination rather than the eyes

explanation.surface: Picture spotting an object in your own head.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the faculty of mental imagery, where we picture things that are not present.

clue.text: Make pro say 'going west'

parts.note: pro means in favour of, for

indicators.note: in an across entry going west means read from right to left, so the abbreviation is turned round

parts.note: say is the usual crossword signal for EG, for example

explanation.surface: An instruction to make a professional announce that they are heading west.
explanation.definitionFit: To forge is to make or shape something, as a smith shapes metal or a nation forges a bond.

clue.text: Where one may put, given time, car by village area?

definitions.text: Where one may put, given time

indicators.note: by means beside, so the two pieces sit side by side

parts.note: the Golf is a Volkswagen car model
a village green is the common grassy area at a village's centre

explanation.surface: A puzzle about where someone could park, with a car next to the village common.
explanation.walkthrough: Add a T (time) to 'put' and it becomes 'putt', the golf stroke played on a green; the definition hides that extra letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The green is the closely mown area round the hole where golfers putt the ball.

clue.text: I hang out with Pence, which is demeaning

indicators.note: out signals that the letters are put out of their order, a rearrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A speaker admits spending time with Mike Pence, the former US vice president, which they find degrading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' turns I HANG PENCE into the ten letters of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Degrading something lowers its worth or dignity, and demeaning is a synonym in that sense.

clue.text: Tropical fruits lacking male leaves

indicators.note: lacking means without, so the word for male is removed from the fruit

parts.note: mangoes are tropical fruits
a man is a male person

explanation.surface: Some tropical fruit, minus any masculine parts, turns into foliage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' looks like plant foliage beside the fruit but is the verb: departs.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave and to go both mean to depart, so he leaves is he departs.

clue.text: Insanitary hospital locked up by nice guy in cast

indicators.note: locked up by means held inside, so the hospital letter sits within the other letters
cast, as in cast anew or recast, signals that the letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A dirty hospital is imprisoned by a pleasant man wearing a plaster cast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' reads as a plaster cast or a play's cast, but it is the anagram signal; 'in' is part of the fodder, not a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Insanitary and the answer both describe conditions that are dirty and likely to spread disease.

clue.text: Continually add anything different

indicators.note: different indicates the letters are made into something different, a rearrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to keep on adding whatever comes to hand that is unusual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'different' rearranges ADD ANYTHING; the answer is also a Cole Porter song, the puzzle's theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done round the clock, through dark and light alike, is done constantly without a break.

clue.text: Fighter's protection is good, er, to avoid exposure to Covid-19?

parts.note: er and um are both sounds of hesitation
to shield was the term for vulnerable people staying home to avoid catching Covid-19

explanation.surface: A boxer's guard is good, er, for keeping clear of the coronavirus.
explanation.definitionFit: Boxers wear a mouthguard over the teeth to protect them from punches.

clue.text: Darling tenor's intro to Regret Nothing

indicators.note: a word's intro is its opening letter, here from tenor's

parts.note: rue means regret
love means nothing, a score of zero in tennis

explanation.surface: A singer's sweetheart introduces a song called Regret Nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is also the Cole Porter song True Love, part of the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweetheart or beloved is one's darling, the person one loves.

clue.text: An obsession about New York, no matter what

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the obsession phrase goes round the city's letters

parts.note: to have a thing about something is to be obsessed with it

explanation.surface: A fixation regarding New York, whatever happens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like part of 'a thing about' but is the container signal; Anything Goes is a Cole Porter musical.
explanation.definitionFit: Anything at all, as in do whatever it takes, means whatever the case may be.

clue.text: Fancy manors with greens for an extortionate sum

indicators.note: fancy, as an adjective, means elaborate or altered, signalling the word manors is rearranged

parts.note: greens, like greenbacks, is slang for money, from the colour of banknotes

explanation.surface: Smart country houses, plus a vegetable patch, would cost an outrageous price.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' rearranges MANORS into RANSOM.
explanation.definitionFit: Kidnappers demand a large payment for release, and the cash handed over is that payment.

clue.text: Test a plexiglass housing key element

indicators.note: housing means containing, so the words test a plexiglass hold the letters inside them

explanation.surface: Testing a clear acrylic sheet that encloses a vital component.
explanation.definitionFit: A staple is a basic or principal item, as rice is a staple diet.

clue.text: Ruffled father gets mad on losing lead

parts.note: FR is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title

indicators.note: losing lead means dropping the first letter of the word for mad

parts.note: silly means mad in the sense of foolish

explanation.surface: An agitated dad gets angry after falling behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruffled' looks like upset, but it is the dressmaking sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruffled clothing has frills, gathered strips of fabric, so it is frilly.

clue.text: Possibly settles on giving up southern food

indicators.note: giving up means surrendering or dropping, so the southern letter is removed

parts.note: a settle is a wooden bench, so settles are possibly seats; the possibly marks them as examples

explanation.surface: Benches perhaps, set on refusing southern cooking.
explanation.definitionFit: Eats is informal slang for food, as in a sign offering cheap eats.

clue.text: Thief, one's partner, say, taking lead from hellraiser

indicators.note: taking means taking in, so the significant other abbreviation holds the next letter

parts.note: SOP, significant other person, is a term for one's partner; say marks it as an example
the setter splits hellraiser: the lead, or first letter, of its hell half is H
the raiser half of hellraiser is read as one who raises, a lifter

explanation.surface: A crook turns out to be someone's spouse, following a troublemaker's example.
explanation.walkthrough: SOP (significant other person) is a Chambers term few solvers know. 'hellraiser' does double work: 'lead from' takes the first letter of its hell half, and its raiser half supplies the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who steals goods from a store is a particular kind of thief.

clue.text: Crowd downcast with no action outside

indicators.note: with no means without, so the letters of the action word are taken away
outside means those removed letters are on the outside of the word, at both ends

parts.note: downcast means depressed, low in spirits
a deed is an action

explanation.surface: A dejected crowd with nothing happening around them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' tells you the action word is split, its halves coming off both ends of the downcast word.
explanation.definitionFit: To press is to crowd or push in on someone, and a press is also a crowd of people.

clue.text: A brassica, firm and large with edible tip

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

indicators.note: the tip of a word is its first letter, here from edible

explanation.surface: A cabbage-type vegetable, firm and big, with a top you can eat.
explanation.walkthrough: Cole Porter is the theme, so this word is his first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Cole is an old word for cabbage and related plants of the cabbage family.

clue.text: Turning cool in eg end of temperate epoch

indicators.note: turning suggests the letters are turned about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter, taken from temperate

explanation.surface: Cooling, for example, at the close of a mild geological era.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning' rearranges COOL IN EG into OLIGOCEN, and 'end of temperate' adds the last E.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oligocene is a geological epoch of about 34 to 23 million years ago, within the Tertiary period.

clue.text: Pound backed by a Latin country

indicators.note: backed means going backwards, so the word for pound is read in reverse

parts.note: a pound is an enclosure for animals, a pen

explanation.surface: Sterling supported by a Latin-speaking state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pound' looks like money; it is an animal enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: Nepal is a landlocked Himalayan nation between India and China.

clue.text: Intellectual Wren potentially owned Round House's east wing

parts.note: an egg is potentially a wren, since the bird hatches from one

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the word for owned goes around the wing letter

parts.note: owned means had, possessed
the east, or right-hand, end of the word House is its last letter, E

explanation.surface: An architect such as Christopher Wren might have owned the east wing of a round building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wren' suggests the architect Sir Christopher Wren, but here it is the small bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Egghead is an informal, slightly mocking term for a highbrow or academic person.

clue.text: Old revolutionary council about to replace five-year community

indicators.note: to replace means one letter is swapped in where another stood

parts.note: a soviet was a council in revolutionary Russia
V is five in Roman numerals
C stands for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A former Russian committee is about to give way to a five-year plan for the people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'five-year' looks like the Soviet five-year plan, but it splits: five is V, replaced by C, and year adds Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A society is a body of people living together under shared rules, a community.
